skill.name: aws-iam-best-practices
skill.description: Review AWS IAM policies, reduce excessive permissions, and guide least privilege hardening.
skill.summary: Guides IAM policy review, MFA checks, access key hygiene, and least privilege hardening.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, sample AWS CLI commands, documentation URLs, placeholder values, and example CIDR ranges. No prompt injection, covert exfiltration, or malicious intent was found. One medium semantic concern remains because several examples can mutate IAM resources if executed without explicit user approval.

remediation.issue: Mutating IAM examples can change account state if executed without confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit warnings before create-access-key, update-access-key, and create-virtual-mfa-device examples, and require user approval.

remediation.issue: Bash snippets may be mistaken for commands the skill should run automatically.
remediation.suggestion: Label examples as manual commands and separate read-only checks from write actions.

remediation.issue: The MFA QR example writes bootstrap material to a fixed temporary path.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to choose a protected local path and delete QR bootstrap files after enrollment.

semantic_findings.title: Mutating IAM Examples Require User Confirmation
semantic_findings.description: The skill includes examples that create a virtual MFA device, create a new access key, and deactivate an old access key. These are legitimate hardening actions but can change AWS account state if an agent runs them without explicit approval.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited commands directly call AWS IAM write APIs in documented examples. The surrounding context is defensive, so the risk is operational misuse rather than malicious intent.

content.value_statement: IAM permissions can expand over time and expose sensitive cloud resources. This skill helps review policies, reduce excess access, and plan safer IAM hardening.
actual_capabilities: Reviews IAM policy text for wildcard actions, broad resources, missing conditions, and least privilege gaps.
Guides MFA checks, access key age review, role trust review, and unused role discovery.
Provides least privilege patterns for S3, MFA, time-based access, and IP-based controls.
Supplies AWS CLI examples for IAM inventory, policy analysis, and hardening tasks.
Builds an IAM hardening checklist for users, policies, roles, and monitoring.
limitations: It does not verify account state unless the user supplies current data or approved command output.
It is not a replacement for IAM Access Analyzer, policy simulation, or expert cloud security review.
Some examples require IAM permissions and can change account state if executed.
Generated policies must be tested outside production before use.

use_cases.title: Review a Cloud Policy
use_cases.description: Find broad actions, broad resources, missing conditions, and safer alternatives in an IAM policy.

use_cases.title: Prepare Access Key Cleanup
use_cases.description: Identify old access keys and plan a controlled rotation path with validation steps.

use_cases.title: Audit IAM Hardening Gaps
use_cases.description: Create a checklist for MFA, roles, managed policies, monitoring, and regular access reviews.

prompt_templates.title: Review One Policy
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this IAM policy for least privilege, wildcard actions, broad resources, and missing conditions. Return prioritized findings and safer alternatives.

prompt_templates.title: Design S3 Access
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a least privilege IAM approach for S3 read and write access to one bucket prefix per user. Include validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Assess IAM Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this IAM inventory output for users without MFA, old access keys, unused roles, and risky trust relationships.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Hardening Rollout
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a phased IAM hardening plan for multiple AWS accounts. Include risks, owner actions, testing, rollback, and monitoring checks.

output_examples.input: Review an IAM policy that grants broad S3 access.
output: High risk: S3 read and write actions apply too broadly.
Recommendation: limit access to the required bucket and user prefix.
Validation: test the change with IAM Policy Simulator before production.

output_examples.input: Find IAM users that need MFA and access key review.
output: MFA gap: several users have no registered MFA device.
Key hygiene gap: keys older than 90 days need rotation planning.
Next step: confirm owners, rotate in stages, and monitor failed authentication.

output_examples.input: Create a hardening checklist for an AWS account.
output: Users: enable MFA and remove unused accounts.
Policies: replace broad permissions with scoped managed policies.
Monitoring: enable CloudTrail and review IAM changes regularly.

best_practices: Provide current policies, role trust documents, and account constraints before requesting recommendations.
Test suggested policy changes in a non-production account before rollout.
Require explicit approval before running IAM commands that create, update, or delete resources.
anti_patterns: Do not apply generated IAM policies directly to production without simulation and peer review.
Do not use long-term access keys when roles or temporary credentials are practical.
Do not ignore wildcard actions, wildcard resources, or missing MFA conditions.

faq.question: Can this skill run an AWS account audit by itself?
faq.answer: No. It needs user-provided policy data or approved command output to assess current account state.

faq.question: Does it replace AWS IAM Access Analyzer?
faq.answer: No. Use Access Analyzer and policy simulation to validate findings and proposed changes.

faq.question: Can it create least privilege policies?
faq.answer: Yes. It can draft scoped policy approaches based on the resources, actions, and conditions you provide.

faq.question: Are the command examples safe to run?
faq.answer: Some commands only read IAM data, while others modify IAM resources. Review each command and approve write actions first.

faq.question: What inputs improve review quality?
faq.answer: Provide IAM policies, role trust documents, intended access, resource names, account boundaries, and relevant compliance needs.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
